svg.text: Part 1 architecture: Oracle SRC to TGT with one-way GoldenGate replication
Three Docker containers on one Windows laptop. Numbers 1 to 7 follow the data flow (legend at the bottom).
Windows laptop: Docker Desktop (4 CPUs and 10.7 GiB RAM available to Docker; no per-container CPU or memory limits set)
Docker network telco-net (user-defined bridge): containers find each other by name, e.g. src-db:1521 and tgt-db:1521
Oracle AI Database 26ai Free 23.26.3.0.0, DB name FREE
Host port 1521 mapped to container port 1521
Charset AL32UTF8; SGA 1.5 GiB; PGA 512 MiB; processes 200
ARCHIVELOG, FORCE LOGGING, supplemental logging ON
FRA 8 GiB; 3 redo groups x 50 MB
workload looks rows up by subscriber_id
no primary key, no index (task rule)
every change is written to the online redo log
full redo groups are archived into the FRA
supplemental logging adds the columns that
identify the row, so Replicat can apply it
GGCAPTURE : GoldenGate capture user, role OGG_CAPTURE
Profile: failed-login limit; default accounts locked
Unified audit of failed logons; no passwords in the repo
GoldenGate never uses SYS or SYSTEM
progress kept in a TGT checkpoint table
Direction is one-way: SRC to TGT only.
SRC and TGT never talk to each other;
target database, receives the replicated data
Oracle AI Database 26ai Free 23.26.3.0.0, DB name FREE
Host port 1522 mapped to container port 1521
Charset AL32UTF8; SGA 1.5 GiB; PGA 512 MiB; processes 200
ARCHIVELOG, FORCE LOGGING; FRA size not set (0)
same structure and partitioning as SRC
each UPDATE / DELETE needs a table scan
this is where the Replicat lag appeared
Checkpoint table (written in the same commit
as the replicated data, so no change is applied twice)
GGAPPLY : GoldenGate apply user, role OGG_APPLY
Same profile: failed-login limit, default accounts locked
GoldenGate never uses SYS or SYSTEM
500 TPS, 16 sessions, 65 minutes, runs inside SRC
The workload (TELCO_LOAD, 500 TPS) runs INSERT / UPDATE on TELCO tables in SRC.
Oracle writes every change into the redo log; full groups are archived into the FRA.
EXT1 connects to src-db:1521 as GGCAPTURE and reads the changes (LogMiner server).
EXT1 writes the changes into trail aa (files inside the gg container).
REP1 reads trail aa (several parallel apply threads).
REP1 connects to tgt-db:1521 as GGAPPLY, applies the changes and commits its checkpoint.
Monitoring: browser to the Administration Service (lag, statistics, status).
